note.question: How do ad valorem contracts allow upstream firms (principals) to preserve their own incentives to make ongoing investments in the channel and deal with pricing distortions caused by channel coordination problems, while at the same time adjusting their investment on the basis of demand shocks that are only observed by the downstream firms (agents)?
note.overview: We provide a new theory of ad valorem contracts (i.e., contracts that vary with the value of the transaction), which can explain why such contracts are widely used between vertically related parties (e.g., in franchising and licensing). Ad valorem contracts allow upstream firms (principals) to preserve their own incentives to make ongoing investments in the channel and deal with pricing distortions caused by channel coordination problems, while at the same time adjusting their investment on the basis of demand shocks that are only observed by the downstream firms (agents). This paper was accepted by Eric Anderson, marketing.
